text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Leftist opposition leader Deniz Baykal praises the Turkish media after media members were injured in an Islamist protest.
MILLIYET
- Government accuses Islamist Welfare Party of being behind protest by thousands of Islamists opposing plans to curtail religious education.
- A protocol is signed between the treasury and the central bank to develop a joint monetary policy to combat inflation.
HURRIYET
- The head of the general staff gave the first signs of disbanding a special unit formed in the army to monitor Islamist activism.
- State minister Gunes Taner says operation will be launched to improve the status of the state-owned Ziraat Bank status.
YENI YUZYIL
- Islamists prepare to hold protests against secularist education reforms every day after noon prayer at mosques.
- Government gearing up to announce extra taxes on certain products to raise 60 trillion lira ($9,500,000) for the education plans.
CUMHURIYET
- Turkish armed forces brief the media.
RADIKAL
- The government follows recipies of International Monetary Fund by its recent pay rises.
DUNYA
- The ban on importing animals for breeding is lifted as of Friday.
ZAMAN
- Ankara police arrest six in an Islamist protest against a secularist education plan and release 60 others who were detained.
($1 = 159,500 Turkish lira)
